findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: A Label probes probe cell that legitimately wraps a shell pipeline example in a backtick code span (a valid GFM table row, since a pipe inside a code span isn't a cell delimiter) is rejected: naive awk -F'|' splitting produces NF=5, not 4, and the row is reported as malformed.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:37 — awk -F'|' splits on every literal pipe
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:41 — row processed without ignoring pipes inside backtick spans
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:44 — if (NF != 4) fires on a valid row (NF=5), reporting it invalid

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: An unclosed ```bash fence under Brief probes is not flagged: the extraction has no heading-boundary reset so it swallows later sections, and if that swallowed prose happens to parse as valid bash (comments/plain words usually do), bash -n reports no error and the malformed pack passes as valid.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:59 — BRIEF_HAS_FENCE only checks for an opening fence, not closure
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:63 — BRIEF_BLOCK awk has no /^## /{f=0} reset, so it swallows past ## Dependencies when unclosed
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:65-66 — bash -n on swallowed prose typically parses cleanly, so BRIEF_ERR stays empty

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: The same unclosed Brief probes ```bash fence also defeats the D4 citation check: the fence-toggle flips 'in fence' at the unclosed opener and never flips back, so a genuine unwrapped citation later in the document (e.g. in ## Dependencies) is excluded from the scan and never flagged.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:63 — the unclosed ```bash fence never hits a matching close
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:74 — STRIPPED's f=!f toggle stays 'in fence' through EOF once unmatched
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:76-77 — bare-citation scan runs only on STRIPPED, so a real unwrapped citation later in the doc is never reported

findings.label: validation
findings.failure_mode: A plain URL mentioned in prose outside any fence (e.g. https://docs.python.org/3/library/re.html) is wrongly flagged as an unwrapped file citation because the regex's character class excludes ':', so matching resumes right after 'https:' and matches the '//...' remainder as a path-shaped token.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:74 — STRIPPED keeps non-fenced prose including URL mentions
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:76 — grep -oE regex matches '//docs.python.org/3/library/re.html' since ':' isn't in the class
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:77 — grep -v '^`' | grep '/' does not exclude the fragment
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:83 — fail() reports the URL fragment as a bad citation

findings.label: duplication
findings.failure_mode: The Brief probes fenced-```bash block extraction (the awk one-liner that finds the ```bash fence after '## Brief probes' and captures everything up to the closing ```) is hand-copied verbatim into validate-pack.sh instead of being sourced from one shared location. If the pack's Brief-probes fence shape ever needs a fix (e.g. tolerating a different fence marker, or a heading edge case), a change made only in build-artifacts.sh's copy leaves validate-pack.sh silently validating against the old shape, so it can report a pack 'valid' that build-artifacts.sh actually mis-extracts (or reject one it handles fine) with no signal that the two disagree.
evidence: .claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:65 — BRIEF_BLOCK=$(awk '/^## Brief probes/{f=1;next} f&&/^```bash/{b=1;next} f&&b&&/^```/{exit} f&&b' "$PACK")

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/build-artifacts.sh:351 — PROBES="$(awk '/^## Brief probes/{f=1;next} f&&/^```bash/{b=1;next} f&&b&&/^```/{exit} f&&b' "$PACK")" — the identical awk expression, hand-copied rather than sourced from one place

.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:67 — bash -n is run only against validate-pack.sh's own private copy of the extraction, so this validator cannot catch a drift between its copy and build-artifacts.sh's copy — exactly the failure the validator exists to prevent
